messages:
incident-bot: Paging @Anya @Devin @Maya on-call: detected suspicious outbound traffic from log-forwarder-prod -> potential leakage of auth headers. Rule fired: anomaly-egress-2026-03-15. Please triage and ack.
Anya Rivera: acked. I'm looking at the alert now.
Devin Park: on it, pulling logs. not seeing obvious error spikes in runtime yet.
Samir Patel: who owns the forwarder credential rotation? tagging infra-keys but adding here too.
Maya Chen: I can assist with immediate ACLs. Do we know which bucket/endpoint is being targeted?
Anya Rivera: initial alert shows repeated PUTs to s3://redwood-logs-exports from ip 54.193.22.11 via forwarder pod ff-logs-7c9. Headers include x-auth-session header in payload (redacted in alert).
Devin Park: running quick grep on forwarded payloads. output:```
2026-03-15T10:04:02Z ff-logs-7c9 PUT /export/2026/03/15/part-0001.gz headers: {x-auth-session: REDACTED, user: svc-forwarder}
2026-03-15T10:04:05Z ff-logs-7c9 PUT /export/2026/03/15/part-0002.gz headers: {x-auth-session: REDACTED}
```
Anya Rivera: that x-auth-session looks like an internal cookie. could be sensitive. Let's kill the forwarder egress and rotate tokens.
Jonah Laird: proposed immediate mitigations: 1) block egress from ff-logs pods to s3 wildcard, 2) suspend forwarder service account keys, 3) rotate any exposed svc tokens, 4) disable log export pipeline until validated. Agree? :warning:
Maya Chen: agree. I'll apply a temporary NetworkPolicy to block egress to S3 endpoints from the forwarder namespace. Doing now.
Maya Chen: applied NP:```
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: block-forwarder-egress-temp
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ff-logs
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: []
```
Maya Chen: NP applied. Confirming no new PUTs after 10:07:14.
Devin Park: good. I'm listing uploads from that IP to enumerate scope: `aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-logs-exports --prefix export/2026/03/15/ --query 'Contents[].Key'`
Anya Rivera: also create a deny WAF rule for that source ip and similar CIDR, and add to incident timeline.
Samir Patel: rotating keys now for service account `svc-forwarder-prod`. Steps: 1) create new key pair, 2) update forwarder config to use new key, 3) revoke old key. I'll do key create and update CI.
Samir Patel: new key created, updating deployment secret with new key. Will trigger redeploy.
incident-bot: deploy-bot: Deployment ff-logs updated -> rollout started (ff-logs-7c9 -> ff-logs-8a3).
Devin Park: pulled a sample of the exported objects. Confirmed 3 files containing partial stack traces and what looks like truncated auth headers. Nothing appears to be user PII but auth tokens present.
Anya Rivera: customer impact check: which services accept that auth header? Search shows internal service auth used by some staging integration tests and one legacy partner. Reach out to CS to confirm partner exposure.
customer-success-bot: Notifying cs-team and partner-ops@partnerco with templated notice.
Maya Chen: rotating on-platform sessions: issuing revoke for session-token K in KVS and incrementing session salt to invalidate all short-lived sessions. Command: `redis-cli -h sessions.prod INCR session_salt`
Maya Chen: done. Noted some customers on legacy partner might need new auth handshake.
Samir Patel: old key revoked. Confirming s3 PUTs stopped after NP + key rotation.
Devin Park: collecting forensic artifacts: forwarding object copies to secure bucket `sec-forensics-3132109999` with restricted ACL. Also saving pod logs, network flow logs, and AWS CloudTrail entries for the timeframe.
Anya Rivera: quick root-cause hypothesis: forwarder was misconfigured to include full request headers (including internal auth) in export payload. That config change likely deployed earlier today by automation. Need to audit the deploy pipeline.
Jonah Laird: action items: 1) patch forwarder to sanitize headers before export (Anya), 2) add CI gate to prevent header dumps (Devin), 3) rotate keys and invalidate sessions (Samir/Maya), 4) notify affected partner (CS bot), 5) follow-up postmortem and rollback of the automation change (Jonah).
Anya Rivera: creating a quick patch branch now.```
git checkout -b fix/strip-headers
# remove header dump in exporter
```
Anya Rivera: patch pushed and PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/ff-logs/pull/342. Requesting urgent review.
Devin Park: adding a unit test to assert exported payloads do not include sensitive headers. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/ff-logs/pull/343
customer-success-bot: Partner ops request acknowledged. partnerco confirmed they received no customer-identifying data but will rotate any stored tokens as precaution.
Samir Patel: creating post-rotation checklist in runbook: https://runbooks.internal/incidents/log-forwarder-egress-2026. Please add validation steps.
Maya Chen: marking incident as mitigated for live traffic after NP+rotation. Will keep pipeline paused until PR merged and validated in staging.
Anya Rivera: handing off to night team: Devin will own initial postmortem draft and Maya will own validated rollout tomorrow morning. Please follow links and add notes.
Devin Park: taking handoff. timeline and checklist saved in the channel thread. I'll open the postmortem doc and start a short Incident Report.
Jonah Laird: thumbs up. Great triage. Leave incident in incidents channel and set reminder for 12h follow-up.
incident-bot: reminder set for 12h.
Devin Park: final note for handoff: affected artifacts: `export/2026/03/15/part-0001.gz`, `part-0002.gz`, `part-0003.gz`. Forensics copies in `sec-forensics-3132109999`.
Maya Chen: thanks team. I'm going offline in 10. ping me if anything re-emerges.
Anya Rivera: closing loop: PR merged to main at 12:34 UTC, forwarder redeployed with sanitized exports, CI gate added. Will draft RCA tomorrow.
customer-success-bot: Notified partnerco of mitigation and remediation steps. They confirmed ticket closed on their side. :white_check_mark:
